newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan's sugar output falls sharply.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan's sugar output falls sharply.

text.p: The Pakistan Sugar Mills Association said on Sunday sugar production by November 30 in the 1996/97 year (July-June) fell 60.57 percent to 153,656 tonnes compared to 389,731 tonnes in the year-ago period.
The Association gave no reason for the fall, but one dealer attributed it to the late start of sugarcane crushing season in November instead of October.
Pakistan is likely to produce 2.65 million tonnes in 1996/97, compared to 2.47 million in 1995/96 and 3.0 million in 1994/95.

On reports of the shortfall, the state-run Trading Corp of Pakistan invited tenders by December 21 for the import of 50,000 tonnes for shipment by January 11. It had scrapped its earlier tender, which was opened on December 7 for 50,000 tonnes of sugar, an official said. -- Karachi newsroom 9221-5685192
